import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 4.72

by A. L. Shmel'kin

Is it true that every variety of groups whose free groups are residually nilpotent
torsion-free, is either soluble or coincides with the variety of all groups? For an
affirmative answer, it is sufficient to show that every variety of Lie algebras over the
field of rational numbers which does not contain any finite-dimensional simple algebras is
soluble.

A variety of groups is the class of all groups satisfying a set of laws $W$, where a law is
an element of the free group $F_\infty$ on countably many variables $x_0, x_1, \dots$; by
Birkhoff's theorem these are exactly the classes of groups closed under subgroups,
homomorphic images and arbitrary direct products. The free groups of the variety
$\mathfrak{V}(W)$ are the relatively free groups $F_X / W(F_X)$, where $W(F_X)$ is the verbal
subgroup of $F_X$ determined by $W$. "Residually nilpotent torsion-free" is read as
residually (torsion-free nilpotent), and a variety is soluble if it satisfies a solubility
law $\delta_n = 1$ for some fixed $n$. Varieties of Lie algebras over $\mathbb{Q}$ are treated
in the same way, with identities taken in the free Lie algebra on countably many generators.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/
namespace Kourovka.«4.72»
section Groups

blocks.code:
def SatisfiesLaws (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ w ∈ W, ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1
blocks.docstring:
A group `G` *satisfies the laws* `W ⊆ FreeGroup ℕ` if every word `w ∈ W` in the variables
$x_0, x_1, \dots$ takes only the value $1$ in `G`, i.e. $w(g_0, g_1, \dots) = 1$ for every
assignment $x_i \mapsto g_i$ of the variables. The class of all groups satisfying `W` is the
variety of groups $\mathfrak{V}(W)$ defined by `W`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: FreeGroup.lift (used); no variety/law concept in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib (rg for 'variet', 'verbal', 'law' found nothing relevant).
justification.name: Kourovka.«4.72».SatisfiesLaws
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no notion of a group satisfying a law / variety of groups. Defined as: every w ∈ W ⊆ FreeGroup ℕ maps to 1 under FreeGroup.lift f for every assignment f : ℕ → G.

blocks.name: SatisfiesLaws
blocks.text:
/-- A group `G` *satisfies the laws* `W ⊆ FreeGroup ℕ` if every word `w ∈ W` in the variables
$x_0, x_1, \dots$ takes only the value $1$ in `G`, i.e. $w(g_0, g_1, \dots) = 1$ for every
assignment $x_i \mapsto g_i$ of the variables. The class of all groups satisfying `W` is the
variety of groups $\mathfrak{V}(W)$ defined by `W`. -/
def SatisfiesLaws (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ w ∈ W, ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1

blocks.code:
def verbalSubgroup (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Subgroup G :=
  Subgroup.normalClosure {g | ∃ w ∈ W, ∃ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = g}
blocks.docstring:
The *verbal subgroup* $W(G)$ of `G` determined by the set of words `W`: the subgroup of `G`
generated by all values $w(g_0, g_1, \dots)$ of words $w \in W$ in `G`. This subgroup is
normal (its generating set is closed under conjugation), so we use `Subgroup.normalClosure`
to record that.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Subgroup.normalClosure, Subgroup.closure (no verbal-subgroup notion in Mathlib).
justification.name: Kourovka.«4.72».verbalSubgroup (+ instance verbalSubgroup_normal)
justification.why_needed: The verbal subgroup W(G) is needed to build relatively free groups F_X / W(F_X). Defined as Subgroup.normalClosure of the set of values of words of W (the set is conjugation-closed, so this equals the ordinary closure; normalClosure gives the Normal instance directly).

instance verbalSubgroup_normal (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (G : Type*) [Group G] :
    (verbalSubgroup W G).Normal :=

blocks.code:
abbrev RelativelyFreeGroup (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (X : Type*) : Type _ :=
  FreeGroup X ⧸ verbalSubgroup W (FreeGroup X)
blocks.docstring:
The (relatively) free group of the variety $\mathfrak{V}(W)$ on the set `X` of free
generators, namely $F_X / W(F_X)$ where $F_X$ is the (absolutely) free group on `X`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: FreeGroup, QuotientGroup (no relatively free group in Mathlib).
justification.name: Kourovka.«4.72».RelativelyFreeGroup
justification.why_needed: The free groups of the variety 𝔙(W) are F_X / W(F_X); abbrev for FreeGroup X ⧸ verbalSubgroup W (FreeGroup X). A test lemma checks it satisfies the laws W.

blocks.name: RelativelyFreeGroup
blocks.text:
/-- The (relatively) free group of the variety $\mathfrak{V}(W)$ on the set `X` of free
generators, namely $F_X / W(F_X)$ where $F_X$ is the (absolutely) free group on `X`. -/
abbrev RelativelyFreeGroup (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (X : Type*) : Type _ :=
  FreeGroup X ⧸ verbalSubgroup W (FreeGroup X)

blocks.docstring:
A group `G` is *residually torsion-free nilpotent* if for every $g \neq 1$ in `G` there is a
normal subgroup $N$ of `G` with $g \notin N$ such that the quotient $G / N$ is nilpotent and
torsion-free (has no nontrivial elements of finite order).

justification.closest_existing_considered: Group.IsNilpotent (used), IsMulTorsionFree (deliberately not used: for non-abelian groups it is the stronger unique-roots property, equivalent to torsion-freeness for nilpotent groups only via Mal'cev's theorem), IsOfFinOrder (used).
justification.name: Kourovka.«4.72».IsResiduallyTorsionFreeNilpotent
justification.why_needed: No residual-property notion in Mathlib. Defined as: for every g ≠ 1 there is a normal N with g ∉ N, G ⧸ N nilpotent, and every nontrivial element of G ⧸ N of infinite order.

blocks.name: IsResiduallyTorsionFreeNilpotent
blocks.text:
/-- A group `G` is *residually torsion-free nilpotent* if for every $g \neq 1$ in `G` there is a
normal subgroup $N$ of `G` with $g \notin N$ such that the quotient $G / N$ is nilpotent and
torsion-free (has no nontrivial elements of finite order). -/
def IsResiduallyTorsionFreeNilpotent (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ (N : Subgroup G) (_ : N.Normal),
    g ∉ N ∧ Group.IsNilpotent (G ⧸ N) ∧ ∀ x : G ⧸ N, x ≠ 1 → ¬ IsOfFinOrder x

blocks.code:
def IsSolubleVariety (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) : Prop :=
  ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], SatisfiesLaws W G → derivedSeries G n = ⊥
blocks.docstring:
The variety of groups $\mathfrak{V}(W)$ is *soluble* if it satisfies a solubility law
$\delta_n = 1$ for some fixed $n$, i.e. there is an $n$ such that every group in
$\mathfrak{V}(W)$ is soluble of derived length at most $n$.

justification.name: Kourovka.«4.72».IsSolubleVariety
justification.why_needed: Soluble variety = satisfies a solubility law δ_n = 1: ∃ n, every group satisfying W has derivedSeries G n = ⊥ (uniform bound, as the decomposition notes require).

blocks.name: IsSolubleVariety
blocks.text:
/-- The variety of groups $\mathfrak{V}(W)$ is *soluble* if it satisfies a solubility law
$\delta_n = 1$ for some fixed $n$, i.e. there is an $n$ such that every group in
$\mathfrak{V}(W)$ is soluble of derived length at most $n$. -/
def IsSolubleVariety (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) : Prop :=
  ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], SatisfiesLaws W G → derivedSeries G n = ⊥

blocks.code:
def IsVarietyOfAllGroups (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], SatisfiesLaws W G
blocks.docstring:
The variety of groups $\mathfrak{V}(W)$ coincides with the variety of all groups, i.e.
every group satisfies the laws `W`.

justification.name: Kourovka.«4.72».IsVarietyOfAllGroups
justification.why_needed: 'Coincides with the variety of all groups': every group satisfies the laws W.

blocks.name: IsVarietyOfAllGroups
blocks.text:
/-- The variety of groups $\mathfrak{V}(W)$ coincides with the variety of all groups, i.e.
every group satisfies the laws `W`. -/
def IsVarietyOfAllGroups (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], SatisfiesLaws W G

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isResiduallyTorsionFreeNilpotent_of_torsionFree (G : Type*) [Group G]
    [Group.IsNilpotent G] (hG : ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ¬ IsOfFinOrder g) :
    IsResiduallyTorsionFreeNilpotent G := by
  intro g hg
  refine ⟨⊥, inferInstance, by simpa using hg, ?_, fun x hx ↦ ?_⟩
  · exact (Group.isNilpotent_congr (QuotientGroup.quotientBot (G := G)).symm).mp inferInstance
  · rw [← (QuotientGroup.quotientBot (G := G)).injective.isOfFinOrder_iff]
    exact hG _ fun h ↦ hx ((QuotientGroup.quotientBot (G := G)).map_eq_one_iff.mp h)
blocks.docstring: Torsion-free nilpotent groups are residually torsion-free nilpotent.

    [Group.IsNilpotent G] (hG : ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ¬ IsOfFinOrder g) :
    IsResiduallyTorsionFreeNilpotent G := by
  intro g hg
  refine ⟨⊥, inferInstance, by simpa using hg, ?_, fun x hx ↦ ?_⟩
  · exact (Group.isNilpotent_congr (QuotientGroup.quotientBot (G := G)).symm).mp inferInstance
  · rw [← (QuotientGroup.quotientBot (G := G)).injective.isOfFinOrder_iff]

blocks.code:
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem satisfiesLaws_relativelyFreeGroup (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (X : Type*) :
    SatisfiesLaws W (RelativelyFreeGroup W X) := by
  intro w hw f
  choose f' hf' using fun i ↦ QuotientGroup.mk_surjective (f i)
  rw [← FreeGroup.lift_unique ((QuotientGroup.mk' _).comp (FreeGroup.lift f')) (by simp [hf'])]
  exact (QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff _).mpr (Subgroup.subset_normalClosure ⟨w, hw, f', rfl⟩)
blocks.docstring: The relatively free group of the variety $\mathfrak{V}(W)$ lies in $\mathfrak{V}(W)$.
blocks.name: satisfiesLaws_relativelyFreeGroup
blocks.text:
/-- The relatively free group of the variety $\mathfrak{V}(W)$ lies in $\mathfrak{V}(W)$. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem satisfiesLaws_relativelyFreeGroup (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (X : Type*) :
    SatisfiesLaws W (RelativelyFreeGroup W X) := by
  intro w hw f
  choose f' hf' using fun i ↦ QuotientGroup.mk_surjective (f i)
  rw [← FreeGroup.lift_unique ((QuotientGroup.mk' _).comp (FreeGroup.lift f')) (by simp [hf'])]
  exact (QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff _).mpr (Subgroup.subset_normalClosure ⟨w, hw, f', rfl⟩)

def LieSatisfiesIdentities (W : Set (FreeLieAlgebra ℚ ℕ)) (L : Type*) [LieRing L]
    [LieAlgebra ℚ L] : Prop :=
  ∀ w ∈ W, ∀ f : ℕ → L, FreeLieAlgebra.lift ℚ f w = 0
blocks.docstring:
A Lie algebra `L` over `ℚ` *satisfies the identities* `W ⊆ FreeLieAlgebra ℚ ℕ` if every
element `w ∈ W` of the free Lie algebra on the generators $x_0, x_1, \dots$ vanishes under every
assignment $x_i \mapsto l_i$ of the generators to elements of `L`. The class of all Lie algebras
over `ℚ` satisfying `W` is the variety of Lie algebras $\mathfrak{V}(W)$ defined by `W`.

justification.why_needed: No variety-of-Lie-algebras notion in Mathlib. Defined as: every w ∈ W ⊆ FreeLieAlgebra ℚ ℕ maps to 0 under FreeLieAlgebra.lift ℚ f for every assignment f : ℕ → L.

/-- A Lie algebra `L` over `ℚ` *satisfies the identities* `W ⊆ FreeLieAlgebra ℚ ℕ` if every

def LieSatisfiesIdentities (W : Set (FreeLieAlgebra ℚ ℕ)) (L : Type*) [LieRing L]
    [LieAlgebra ℚ L] : Prop :=
  ∀ w ∈ W, ∀ f : ℕ → L, FreeLieAlgebra.lift ℚ f w = 0

blocks.docstring:
The variety of Lie algebras $\mathfrak{V}(W)$ over `ℚ` is *soluble* if it satisfies a
solubility identity $\delta_n = 0$ for some fixed $n$, i.e. there is an $n$ such that every Lie
algebra in $\mathfrak{V}(W)$ is soluble of derived length at most $n$.

justification.name: Kourovka.«4.72».IsSolubleLieVariety
justification.why_needed: Soluble variety of Lie algebras: ∃ n, every Lie algebra over ℚ satisfying W has LieAlgebra.derivedSeries ℚ L n = ⊥.

blocks.name: IsSolubleLieVariety
blocks.text:
/-- The variety of Lie algebras $\mathfrak{V}(W)$ over `ℚ` is *soluble* if it satisfies a
solubility identity $\delta_n = 0$ for some fixed $n$, i.e. there is an $n$ such that every Lie
algebra in $\mathfrak{V}(W)$ is soluble of derived length at most $n$. -/
def IsSolubleLieVariety (W : Set (FreeLieAlgebra ℚ ℕ)) : Prop :=
  ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ (L : Type) [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra ℚ L],
    LieSatisfiesIdentities W L → LieAlgebra.derivedSeries ℚ L n = ⊥

blocks.docstring:
The variety of Lie algebras $\mathfrak{V}(W)$ over `ℚ` contains no finite-dimensional
simple Lie algebra. Here simple means non-abelian with no nontrivial proper ideals, as in
`LieAlgebra.IsSimple`; this excludes the one-dimensional (abelian) Lie algebra, which lies in
every nontrivial variety.

justification.name: Kourovka.«4.72».LieVarietyHasNoFiniteDimensionalSimple
justification.why_needed: 'Does not contain any finite-dimensional simple algebras': no L with FiniteDimensional ℚ L and LieAlgebra.IsSimple ℚ L satisfies W.

blocks.name: LieVarietyHasNoFiniteDimensionalSimple
blocks.text:
/-- The variety of Lie algebras $\mathfrak{V}(W)$ over `ℚ` contains no finite-dimensional
simple Lie algebra. Here simple means non-abelian with no nontrivial proper ideals, as in
`LieAlgebra.IsSimple`; this excludes the one-dimensional (abelian) Lie algebra, which lies in
every nontrivial variety. -/
def LieVarietyHasNoFiniteDimensionalSimple (W : Set (FreeLieAlgebra ℚ ℕ)) : Prop :=
  ∀ (L : Type) [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra ℚ L],
    FiniteDimensional ℚ L → LieAlgebra.IsSimple ℚ L → ¬ LieSatisfiesIdentities W L

claims.decomposer_note: Yes/no question (answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ varieties …); 'variety' is a Birkhoff class (closed under subgroups, quotients, arbitrary direct products, equivalently defined by laws — no Mathlib definition exists), 'free groups' means the relatively free groups of the variety of every rank, 'residually nilpotent torsion-free' should be read as residually (torsion-free nilpotent), and a 'soluble variety' means one satisfying a solubility law of some fixed derived length (uniformly bounded), not merely that each member is soluble.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state this slot faithfully in essentially the same way (variety = class defined by a set of laws W in FreeGroup ℕ, relatively free groups F_X/W(F_X) for every rank X : Type, residually (torsion-free nilpotent), soluble = one uniform derived length, 'all groups' = every group satisfies W). c03 was chosen because it uses the literal torsion-free condition (no nontrivial element of finite order) rather than Mathlib's IsMulTorsionFree (unique roots; equivalent for nilpotent groups only via Mal'cev's theorem, used by c01/c05/c06/c07/c08), builds the relatively free group explicitly via the verbal subgroup (more transparent than c05's universal-property existential or c06's semantic word-separation encoding), gives named bespoke predicates, and ships proven test lemmas (including that relatively free groups lie in their variety and that TFN groups are residually TFN). c04 and c08 are equally faithful alternatives; c02 also faithful. Universe: quantifying members over Type is harmless since laws are detected by the countable-rank relatively free group.
claims.source_text: Is it true that every variety of groups whose free groups are residually nilpotent torsion-free, is either soluble or coincides with the variety of all groups?

claims.decomposer_note: Subordinate stronger form (a sufficient condition) stated as a definite Prop: every variety of Lie algebras over ℚ containing no finite-dimensional simple (i.e. non-abelian, as in Mathlib's LieAlgebra.IsSimple) Lie algebra satisfies a solubility identity of some fixed derived length; the implication 'this ⇒ the group question' is asserted as known rather than posed, so only the Lie-algebra claim itself is formalized.
claims.reviewer_why: All candidates faithfully state: for every set W of identities in FreeLieAlgebra ℚ ℕ, if no finite-dimensional L with LieAlgebra.IsSimple ℚ L (non-abelian) satisfies W, then some fixed n has LieAlgebra.derivedSeries ℚ L n = ⊥ for every L in the variety. c03's version was kept for consistency with the group slot's definitions; I edited its docstrings to spell out the reading of 'simple' (non-abelian, as in LieAlgebra.IsSimple — excluding the 1-dimensional abelian algebra, which would make the hypothesis vacuous) and 'soluble', and changed the AMS tag to 17 20 (Lie-algebra claim arising from a group-theory problem, as in c02/c04/c08). Only the Lie claim is asserted; the notebook's sufficiency implication is mentioned in the docstring only, per the decomposition table.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 4.72

by A. L. Shmel'kin

Is it true that every variety of groups whose free groups are residually nilpotent
torsion-free, is either soluble or coincides with the variety of all groups? For an
affirmative answer, it is sufficient to show that every variety of Lie algebras over the
field of rational numbers which does not contain any finite-dimensional simple algebras is
soluble.

A variety of groups is the class of all groups satisfying a set of laws $W$, where a law is
an element of the free group $F_\infty$ on countably many variables $x_0, x_1, \dots$; by
Birkhoff's theorem these are exactly the classes of groups closed under subgroups,
homomorphic images and arbitrary direct products. The free groups of the variety
$\mathfrak{V}(W)$ are the relatively free groups $F_X / W(F_X)$, where $W(F_X)$ is the verbal
subgroup of $F_X$ determined by $W$. "Residually nilpotent torsion-free" is read as
residually (torsion-free nilpotent), and a variety is soluble if it satisfies a solubility
law $\delta_n = 1$ for some fixed $n$. Varieties of Lie algebras over $\mathbb{Q}$ are treated
in the same way, with identities taken in the free Lie algebra on countably many generators.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«4.72»

section Groups

/-- A group `G` *satisfies the laws* `W ⊆ FreeGroup ℕ` if every word `w ∈ W` in the variables
$x_0, x_1, \dots$ takes only the value $1$ in `G`, i.e. $w(g_0, g_1, \dots) = 1$ for every
assignment $x_i \mapsto g_i$ of the variables. The class of all groups satisfying `W` is the
variety of groups $\mathfrak{V}(W)$ defined by `W`. -/
def SatisfiesLaws (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ w ∈ W, ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1

/-- The *verbal subgroup* $W(G)$ of `G` determined by the set of words `W`: the subgroup of `G`
generated by all values $w(g_0, g_1, \dots)$ of words $w \in W$ in `G`. This subgroup is
normal (its generating set is closed under conjugation), so we use `Subgroup.normalClosure`
to record that. -/
def verbalSubgroup (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Subgroup G :=
  Subgroup.normalClosure {g | ∃ w ∈ W, ∃ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = g}

instance verbalSubgroup_normal (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (G : Type*) [Group G] :
    (verbalSubgroup W G).Normal :=
  Subgroup.normalClosure_normal

/-- The (relatively) free group of the variety $\mathfrak{V}(W)$ on the set `X` of free
generators, namely $F_X / W(F_X)$ where $F_X$ is the (absolutely) free group on `X`. -/
abbrev RelativelyFreeGroup (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (X : Type*) : Type _ :=
  FreeGroup X ⧸ verbalSubgroup W (FreeGroup X)

/-- A group `G` is *residually torsion-free nilpotent* if for every $g \neq 1$ in `G` there is a
normal subgroup $N$ of `G` with $g \notin N$ such that the quotient $G / N$ is nilpotent and
torsion-free (has no nontrivial elements of finite order). -/
def IsResiduallyTorsionFreeNilpotent (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ (N : Subgroup G) (_ : N.Normal),
    g ∉ N ∧ Group.IsNilpotent (G ⧸ N) ∧ ∀ x : G ⧸ N, x ≠ 1 → ¬ IsOfFinOrder x

/-- The variety of groups $\mathfrak{V}(W)$ is *soluble* if it satisfies a solubility law
$\delta_n = 1$ for some fixed $n$, i.e. there is an $n$ such that every group in
$\mathfrak{V}(W)$ is soluble of derived length at most $n$. -/
def IsSolubleVariety (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) : Prop :=
  ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], SatisfiesLaws W G → derivedSeries G n = ⊥

/-- The variety of groups $\mathfrak{V}(W)$ coincides with the variety of all groups, i.e.
every group satisfies the laws `W`. -/
def IsVarietyOfAllGroups (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], SatisfiesLaws W G

/-- The empty set of laws defines the variety of all groups. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isVarietyOfAllGroups_empty : IsVarietyOfAllGroups ∅ := by
  simp [IsVarietyOfAllGroups, SatisfiesLaws]

/-- Abelian groups satisfy the commutator law $[x_0, x_1] = 1$. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem satisfiesLaws_commutator_of_commGroup (G : Type*) [CommGroup G] :
    SatisfiesLaws {⁅FreeGroup.of 0, FreeGroup.of 1⁆} G := by
  simp [SatisfiesLaws, map_commutatorElement, commutatorElement_eq_one_iff_commute, Commute.all]

/-- The verbal subgroup determined by the empty set of words is trivial. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem verbalSubgroup_empty (G : Type*) [Group G] : verbalSubgroup ∅ G = ⊥ :=
  le_bot_iff.mp (Subgroup.normalClosure_le_normal (by simp))

/-- Torsion-free nilpotent groups are residually torsion-free nilpotent. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isResiduallyTorsionFreeNilpotent_of_torsionFree (G : Type*) [Group G]
    [Group.IsNilpotent G] (hG : ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ¬ IsOfFinOrder g) :
    IsResiduallyTorsionFreeNilpotent G := by
  intro g hg
  refine ⟨⊥, inferInstance, by simpa using hg, ?_, fun x hx ↦ ?_⟩
  · exact (Group.isNilpotent_congr (QuotientGroup.quotientBot (G := G)).symm).mp inferInstance
  · rw [← (QuotientGroup.quotientBot (G := G)).injective.isOfFinOrder_iff]
    exact hG _ fun h ↦ hx ((QuotientGroup.quotientBot (G := G)).map_eq_one_iff.mp h)

/-- The relatively free group of the variety $\mathfrak{V}(W)$ lies in $\mathfrak{V}(W)$. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem satisfiesLaws_relativelyFreeGroup (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (X : Type*) :
    SatisfiesLaws W (RelativelyFreeGroup W X) := by
  intro w hw f
  choose f' hf' using fun i ↦ QuotientGroup.mk_surjective (f i)
  rw [← FreeGroup.lift_unique ((QuotientGroup.mk' _).comp (FreeGroup.lift f')) (by simp [hf'])]
  exact (QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff _).mpr (Subgroup.subset_normalClosure ⟨w, hw, f', rfl⟩)

/--
Is it true that every variety of groups whose free groups are residually nilpotent
torsion-free, is either soluble or coincides with the variety of all groups?

Here the variety is $\mathfrak{V}(W)$ for a set of laws $W \subseteq F_\infty$; its free groups
are the relatively free groups $F_X / W(F_X)$ of every rank; "residually nilpotent torsion-free"
means residually (torsion-free nilpotent); and "soluble" means that the variety satisfies a
solubility law $\delta_n = 1$ for some fixed $n$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«4.72» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ),
      (∀ X : Type, IsResiduallyTorsionFreeNilpotent (RelativelyFreeGroup W X)) →
      IsSolubleVariety W ∨ IsVarietyOfAllGroups W := by
  sorry

end Groups

section LieAlgebras

/-- A Lie algebra `L` over `ℚ` *satisfies the identities* `W ⊆ FreeLieAlgebra ℚ ℕ` if every
element `w ∈ W` of the free Lie algebra on the generators $x_0, x_1, \dots$ vanishes under every
assignment $x_i \mapsto l_i$ of the generators to elements of `L`. The class of all Lie algebras
over `ℚ` satisfying `W` is the variety of Lie algebras $\mathfrak{V}(W)$ defined by `W`. -/
def LieSatisfiesIdentities (W : Set (FreeLieAlgebra ℚ ℕ)) (L : Type*) [LieRing L]
    [LieAlgebra ℚ L] : Prop :=
  ∀ w ∈ W, ∀ f : ℕ → L, FreeLieAlgebra.lift ℚ f w = 0

/-- The variety of Lie algebras $\mathfrak{V}(W)$ over `ℚ` is *soluble* if it satisfies a
solubility identity $\delta_n = 0$ for some fixed $n$, i.e. there is an $n$ such that every Lie
algebra in $\mathfrak{V}(W)$ is soluble of derived length at most $n$. -/
def IsSolubleLieVariety (W : Set (FreeLieAlgebra ℚ ℕ)) : Prop :=
  ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ (L : Type) [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra ℚ L],
    LieSatisfiesIdentities W L → LieAlgebra.derivedSeries ℚ L n = ⊥

/-- The variety of Lie algebras $\mathfrak{V}(W)$ over `ℚ` contains no finite-dimensional
simple Lie algebra. Here simple means non-abelian with no nontrivial proper ideals, as in
`LieAlgebra.IsSimple`; this excludes the one-dimensional (abelian) Lie algebra, which lies in
every nontrivial variety. -/
def LieVarietyHasNoFiniteDimensionalSimple (W : Set (FreeLieAlgebra ℚ ℕ)) : Prop :=
  ∀ (L : Type) [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra ℚ L],
    FiniteDimensional ℚ L → LieAlgebra.IsSimple ℚ L → ¬ LieSatisfiesIdentities W L

/-- The empty set of identities defines the variety of all Lie algebras over `ℚ`. -/
@[category test, AMS 17]
theorem lieSatisfiesIdentities_empty (L : Type*) [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra ℚ L] :
    LieSatisfiesIdentities ∅ L := by
  simp [LieSatisfiesIdentities]

/--
Every variety of Lie algebras over the field of rational numbers which does not contain any
finite-dimensional simple algebras is soluble.

Here a variety of Lie algebras over $\mathbb{Q}$ is $\mathfrak{V}(W)$ for a set of identities
$W$ in the free Lie algebra on countably many generators; "simple" means non-abelian simple, as in
`LieAlgebra.IsSimple`; and "soluble" means that the variety satisfies a solubility identity
$\delta_n = 0$ for some fixed $n$. The Kourovka Notebook states that this suffices for an
affirmative answer to `kourovka.«4.72»`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 17 20]
theorem kourovka.«4.72».variants.lie_algebras :
    ∀ W : Set (FreeLieAlgebra ℚ ℕ),
      LieVarietyHasNoFiniteDimensionalSimple W → IsSolubleLieVariety W := by
  sorry

end LieAlgebras

end Kourovka.«4.72»

items: Varieties are represented equationally (by a set of laws W ⊆ FreeGroup ℕ, resp. identities W ⊆ FreeLieAlgebra ℚ ℕ) rather than as HSP-closed classes; this is the textbook definition (H. Neumann) and is equivalent by Birkhoff's theorem. Different W may define the same variety, which is harmless for a universal statement.

The relatively free group of rank X is modeled as FreeGroup X ⧸ verbalSubgroup W (FreeGroup X); the residual hypothesis is imposed for all X : Type (all ranks, including infinite and empty). Restricting to finite ranks would be equivalent, since a nontrivial element of F_X(𝔙) lies in a finitely generated retract.

'Residually nilpotent torsion-free' is read as residually (torsion-free nilpotent), as the decomposition table prescribes and as the Russian original ('аппроксимируемы нильпотентными группами без кручения') indicates; this differs from 'residually nilpotent and torsion-free' (e.g. the Klein bottle group separates the two).

Torsion-freeness of the quotients is stated literally (no nontrivial element of finite order) instead of Mathlib's IsMulTorsionFree, which for non-abelian groups is the unique-roots property; for nilpotent quotients the two agree by Mal'cev's theorem, but the literal form avoids that dependency.

Soluble variety is formalized with a uniform derived-length bound over all groups (resp. Lie algebras) in the variety, in universe Type. Restricting to Type is harmless: the bound is determined by the countable-rank relatively free object, and finite-dimensional simple ℚ-Lie algebras all have representatives in Type.
'Coincides with the variety of all groups' is formalized as 'every group (in Type) satisfies W', equivalently W ⊆ {1}.

The Lie-algebra slot is stated as a definite Prop (not with answer(sorry)); the notebook's claim that it implies an affirmative answer to the group question is mentioned only in the docstring, per the decomposition table.

Both declarations carry `category research open` following the given status; the file's test lemmas (variety of all groups from ∅, abelian groups satisfy the commutator law, verbal subgroup of ∅ is trivial, torsion-free nilpotent groups are residually TFN, relatively free groups lie in their variety) have short proofs.

reviewer_notes: Final file = c03 with minor docstring edits and AMS 17 20 on the Lie variant; compiles with only 'declaration uses sorry' warnings. Ambiguities: (1) 'residually nilpotent torsion-free' read as residually (torsion-free nilpotent), following the table and the Russian original ('аппроксимируемы нильпотентными группами без кручения'); the alternative reading 'residually nilpotent ∧ torsion-free' is not formalized. (2) 'Soluble variety' uses a uniform derived-length bound; for varieties this is equivalent to every member being soluble (the countable-rank free object is a member), so no real ambiguity. (3) 'Simple' Lie algebra taken as non-abelian simple (Mathlib's IsSimple); with abelian 1-dimensional algebras counted as simple the hypothesis would be unsatisfiable for every nontrivial variety. (4) Varieties are represented by sets of laws (Birkhoff/H. Neumann), all groups/Lie algebras quantified in Type; harmless because the relevant properties are detected by the countable-rank free objects and finite-dimensional ℚ-algebras have representatives in Type. No candidate omitted a slot; no omission reasons to assess. Mathlib's IsMulTorsionFree (used by c01/c05/c06/c07/c08) is 'unique roots', which coincides with torsion-freeness for nilpotent groups only via Mal'cev's theorem — mathematically fine but the literal condition in c03 is preferred.
